Cliopatria's shape for these years lacks Alta California and most of Nevada, Utah and Arizona, which the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo page calls Mexican territories ('Alta California and Santa Fe de Nuevo Mexico', 1.36 M km2 'between the Adams-Onis and Guadalupe Hidalgo boundaries'); they are added; with them the cell count is 15,181 (about 4.5 M km2 on Cliopatria's scale), against the 4.35 M km2 of the Centralist Republic infobox (undated) and the First Mexican Empire's 4.43 M km2. 89 percent of Chiapas is inside, the Soconusco (11 percent) belongs to the Central American shape.

keyframe_review.note: Identical to 1824 (3.19 M km2, 1825-1835): the same lands are added. The Constitution of 1824 came into force on 4 October 1824 and the Spanish fortress of San Juan de Ulua fell in 1825 (Spanish Empire dossier); the Law of 6 April 1830 and the Teran survey of the Texas border (1827-1831) did not change the shape.

Cliopatria draws the core as Centralist Mexico (4,917 cells), a separate row. The shape is kept and Alta California added (the Centralist page gives no list of departments).

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1865 shape is a 166 km2 sliver on the Quintana Roo coast (9 cells), with all of Mexico drawn as its Second Mexican Empire. ledger.note: 1823: the Mexican republic is proclaimed. The infobox says 'Proclaimed: 1 November 1823, by the Supreme Executive Power' and the federation was 'formally and legally established on 4 October 1824'. The Provisional Government of Mexico had taken the empire's lands on 26 March 1823 (First Mexican Empire page).

region.text: Chiapas without the Soconusco claim

ledger.note: 1824: Chiapas is annexed. Chiapas declared its own independence in 1821; 'there was division in the state' in 1823 as to Mexico or Central America, and 'Mexico annexed Chiapas formally in 1824'. The lowlands, including the Soconusco, preferred Central America; Mexico made its first formal claim to the Soconusco in 1825 and took it in 1842.

1824: the Constitution of 1824 comes into force on 4 October. The federation was 'formally and legally established on 4 October 1824'; the constitution confirmed the Roman Catholic religion and established the states.

region.text: the fortress of San Juan de Ulua at Veracruz

ledger.note: 1825: the last Spanish fortress at Veracruz falls. The First Mexican Republic page is silent on San Juan de Ulua; the Spanish Empire dossier dates the loss to 1825 ('Spanish fortifications in Veracruz, Callao and Chiloe resisted until 1825-1826').

region.text: the port of Tampico

ledger.note: 1829: Spain lands at Tampico. The infobox dates the Barradas expedition to July-September 1829: 'Troops were landed at the tropical port of Tampico', where they succumbed to yellow fever.

region.text: the port of Tampico

ledger.note: 1829: the Spanish landing is defeated. The Spaniards at Tampico 'succumbed to yellow fever and were defeated' (infobox: July-September 1829).

region.text: the settled core of Texas that the Republic controlled (Cliopatria's 1836 shape)

ledger.note: 1835: the Texas Revolution begins. 'In the early hours of October 2, approximately 140 Texian volunteers attacked Castaneda's force' at Gonzales (infobox: 2 October 1835 - 21 April 1836).

region.text: the Mexican core under the centralist regime (Cliopatria's Centralist Mexico shape)

ledger.note: 1835: the federal constitution is repealed. The Centralist Republic 'was a unitary political regime established in Mexico on 23 October 1835' (the Siete Leyes); 'conservatives repealed the Constitution of 1824 on 23 October 1835' (First Mexican Republic page). Cliopatria draws the core as its Centralist Mexico row from 1836; the same nation, and the colour agent should keep one hue.

region.text: the settled core of Texas that the Republic controlled (Cliopatria's 1836 shape)

ledger.note: 1836: Texas declares independence on 2 March. 'The declaration passed overwhelmingly on March 2'; the page's infobox result is 'De facto Texian independence from the Centralist Republic of Mexico'. Mexico never recognised it until 1848.

region.text: the settled core of Texas that the Republic controlled (Cliopatria's 1836 shape)

ledger.note: 1836: San Jacinto. 'On April 21, Houston's army staged a surprise assault on Santa Anna' and the Texans 'forced Santa Anna to sign the Treaty of Velasco, which gave Texas its independence'; Santa Anna 'ordered the Mexican army to retreat south of the Rio Grande'.

ledger.note: 1840: the federalists of the north rise. The Republic of the Rio Grande 'was to include the Mexican States of Coahuila, Nuevo Leon, and Tamaulipas'; the rebellion 'lasted from January 17 to November 6, 1840' (Canales surrendered at Camargo). The land returns to the Mexican core row (Centralist Mexico), not to this row.

region.text: the Baja California peninsula

ledger.note: 1853: Walker's filibusters take Baja California. 'On November 3, 1853, the mercenaries proclaimed the independence of the peninsula.' Confidence 2 (reviewer am-08-c): the page says Walker had neither 'full control of the peninsula' nor the support of the population, holding La Paz and then Ensenada.

region.text: the Baja California peninsula

ledger.note: 1854: Walker's Baja California Republic is 'disestablished' on 21 January 1854; he 'surrendered to the US military in San Diego'. The page gives no Mexican reconquest; Cliopatria returns the peninsula in 1856.

ledger.note: 1854: the Gadsden Purchase. 'Santa Anna and Gadsden signed the treaty on December 30, 1853'; the US Senate ratified a revised treaty on 25 April 1854; it 'went into effect June 30, 1854' (June 8 in the infobox): 76,800 km2 of southern Arizona and southwestern New Mexico for US$10 million. Cliopatria shows the loss in 1856.

region.text: Veracruz

ledger.note: 1861: the Tripartite intervention begins. 'On 14 December, Spanish general Juan Prim occupied Mexico's main port, Veracruz, with 6,200 Spanish soldiers from Cuba' (infobox: 8 December 1861 - 21 June 1867).

region.text: Veracruz

ledger.note: 1862: France and Britain join at Veracruz. 'French and British forces joined them on 7 January 1862'; the French stay until 1867.

region.text: Veracruz

ledger.note: 1862: Spain and Britain withdraw. 'The British and Spanish agreed to depart at the same time' (April 1862, from the page's sentence beginning 'On 9 April'); the French remain. On 5 May 1862 Zaragoza and Porfirio Diaz won at Puebla.

region.text: Puebla

ledger.note: 1863: the siege of Puebla. 'The French arrived on 16 March and began the Siege of Puebla'; Gonzalez Ortega 'agreed to surrender on 17 May'.

region.text: Mexico City

ledger.note: 1863: the French occupy Mexico City on 10 June ('the French occupation of Mexico City on 10 June 1863'); Juarez moves the government to San Luis Potosi. The Regency was established on 11 July 1863.

region.text: the central Mexican states held by the Imperialists

ledger.note: 1864: Maximilian's Empire holds the centre. 'Maximilian formally accepted the crown on 10 April 1864'; 'he arrived in Veracruz on 28 May and reached the capital on 12 June'; 'The Imperialists now controlled the central Mexican states, their major cities, two thirds of the population' (French intervention page). The region is Cliopatria's Mexican Monarchists shape, my reading of 'the central states'.

ledger.note: 1864: the Empire takes the northeast. Monterrey 'was captured' on 15 August 1864, 'with Juarez barely escaping'; 'by late 1864 the imperialists controlled Nuevo Leon and most of Coahuila'.

region.text: Chihuahua

ledger.note: 1865: the French enter Chihuahua. 'The French entered Chihuahua City on 15 August 1865, and Juarez fled to El Paso del Norte'; he left 'yet again for the border on 9 December'.

region.text: Mexico City

region.text: Veracruz

ledger.note: 1867: the last French troops embark. 'Bazaine and the last French troops embarked for Toulon on 12 March.' Veracruz is the port; the page does not name it.

region.text: Puebla

ledger.note: 1867: the French leave Puebla with the rest of the army by 12 March (page silent on Puebla).

region.text: Chihuahua

ledger.note: 1867: the French leave Chihuahua with the rest of the army by 12 March (page silent on Chihuahua).

ledger.note: 1867: the Empire falls. Queretaro 'opened the gates to the liberals on 15 May 1867'; 'Maximilian was executed on 19 June'; 'Mexico City surrendered the day after Maximilian's execution'.

ledger.note: 1867: the Republic is restored. Maximilian was executed on 19 June 1867, Mexico City surrendered the next day and 'Juarez returned to the national capital'. The government is continuous; Cliopatria's row ends in 1865 and its 'Mexico' row begins in 1868.

certainty.note: The northern frontier (Alta California, Santa Fe de Nuevo Mexico, Texas) is the Adams-Onis line the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo page names, drawn approximately; the Soconusco boundary with Central America was disputed.
The Texas boundary (Nueces or Rio Grande) was disputed until 1848.
The Rio Grande, Gila and California boundary of the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (1848) and the Gadsden line (1853-1854) are treaty lines; the intervention years (1861-1867) are fronts, not borders.

notes: Cliopatria's row is a regime, not a continuous territory. (1) 1836-1845: the row holds only the northern lands and the land Texas claimed, while a separate row, Centralist Mexico (centralist-mexico, another group; Wikidata Q5062192 shared with 'Mexico'), holds the core. The Centralist Republic page shows one state that changed constitutions (23 October 1835 to 22 August 1846); the two dossiers should keep one colour (family americas) and the 1836 'split' and 1846 'gain' events here are the hand-over between them. (2) Cliopatria draws no Alta California at all before the 1848 cession (only slivers) and only part of Nevada, Utah and Arizona; the keyframes add Alta California and Santa Fe de Nuevo Mexico (the gazetteer regions the United States dossier also uses for the cession). (3) 1862-1865: Cliopatria subtracts the occupied lands and gives the whole of Mexico to its Second Mexican Empire row in 1865, leaving this row a 166 km2 sliver; here Mexico stays sovereign with hatched French and Imperial occupations, and the republican government is continuous with Cliopatria's 'Mexico' row from 1868 (end 1867; the second-mexican-empire and mexican-monarchists dossiers must not also claim the same cells without the occupation reading). (4) The Soconusco (11 percent of Chiapas) is drawn in the Central American shape although Mexico claimed it from 1825; Mexico took it in 1842 (Soconusco page, no month), a gain this dossier does not record because the Federated row's 1842 shape contains no Mexican land. (5) The Gadsden and Baja California events are dated by their pages (1854, 1853-1854) while Cliopatria shifts them to 1856 and 1853-1855. (6) Page budget: nine pages plus the shared Soconusco page and the Baja California page opened for a counterpart event (eleven in all). (7) Not opened: the Reform War (1857-1860), Yucatan's secessions (1841-1843, 1846-1848), the Caste War, the Plan of Cuernavaca and the Zacatecas rebellion of 1835; the Mexican Cession in this dossier's keyframes is Cliopatria's Alta California region, not a surveyed line. (8) The Fed 1836 shape's Texas land is the Texas dossier's contested zone; counterpart dossiers: centralist-mexico, republic-of-texas, republic-of-the-rio-grande, republic-of-baja-california, second-mexican-empire, mexican-monarchists, second-french-empire, mexico, california-republic, united-states-of-america, spanish-empire. (9) The First Mexican Republic page gives no area; the Centralist Republic infobox gives 4.35 M km2 (undated), against about 4.5 M km2 for the corrected 1824 shape (Cliopatria's scale).
